Many of these wastewater streams are similar (although differing in magnitude) to those associated with steam turbine power generating processes. A major difference is the substitution of waste gas liquors (from the gasification process) for that of the stack gas scrubber effluent from power plants. However, the gas liquor effluent is much more complex chemically, and its composition would probably be similar to that of the process liquors derived from the production of coke fuel for the steel industry.
Wastewater treatment would be required to reduce contaminants to acceptable levels before the water could be reused within the plant or released.
The treatment processes employed probably would be similar to those used in petroleum refineries:
1. gravity oil separation with API separators;
dissolved-air flotation with or without addition of flocculating chemicals; and
3. biological treatment
